title.en: Eliza Chan & Sunyi Dean: Hong Kong Ghost Stories

events.description: Two of fantasy’s most exciting voices come together for a captivating conversation exploring ghosts, folklore and the stories that shape us. Bestselling authors Eliza Chan and Sunyi Dean discuss the shared themes running through their acclaimed new novels, from women’s lives and family legacies to memory, identity and generational trauma. Eliza Chan’s Harbour of Hungry Ghosts is a historical fantasy adventure set in Opium War-era Hong Kong, following a family of demon hunters. Sunyi Dean’s The Girl with a Thousand Faces is a haunting dark urban fantasy set during the Japanese occupation of Hong Kong in World War II. Expect a lively discussion on the folklore behind their fiction, writing across cultures and bringing Hong Kong's rich past vividly to life. Co-presented with Waterstones. Eliza Chan is a Scottish-born Chinese-diaspora author who writes across East Asian mythology and British folklore, often exploring identity, reclamation and the power of storytelling. Her novels include Fathomfolk and the sequel Tideborn. She lives in the north of England with her family. Sunyi Dean was born in Texas, raised in Hong Kong and now lives in Yorkshire. Her work is shaped by her personal and family history, including connections to the original Walled City of Kowloon and stories of survival during the Japanese occupation. Mike Diamond, aka Mike D, grew up a precocious and highly opinionated young man on the island of Manhattan. He spent his childhood thieving 7' records by the Jackson Five, The Beatles and various Motown artists from his older brothers while living in the very liberal upper West Side - with the background of New York City's fiscal crisis and all the turmoil and lawlessness that went with that. After finally saving up his own money to purchase Steve Miller's 'Fly Like An Eagle' album, Diamond started to learn to play the drums. Soon after he discovered punk rock and it was game over. That was until he heard a rap mix tape and then it was game over again. Once discovering Reggae through the influence of punk bands like The Clash and The Slits - it was game over a third time. He went on to form Beastie Boys with Adam Yauch, aka MCA, in the early 80's. While inspired by hardcore punk, the boys listened all the while to every new rap 12 inch that came out and eventually rapping themselves. They soon began merging their many influences in what would go on to become a multi-record, multi-platinum and multi-decade career. The band went on to win a bunch awards, such as Grammys, the highly acclaimed Blackshere Award, a very spirited Brass Monkey Award and the key to Kansas City, Missouri... though this is still shrouded in a bit of mystery. In 2012 Beastie Boys were inducted into the Rock N Roll Hall of Fame.

events.description: Based in Ho Chi Minh City, Saigon Soul Revival (SSR) has been bringing alternative pre-1975 music from Saigon back to the stage since 2016. Through electrifying live performances, the band honors the original composers and singers of the golden era of Nhạc Vàng, while applying new compositions and interpretations of old Vietnamese songs. The core lineup consists of five members: Nguyễn Anh Minh (vocals), Indy Jeremy Vinh Laville (guitar & Đàn Nguyệt), Nguyễn Hương Bảo Hiếu (drums), Gabriel Kaouros (bass/percussion), and Đăng Nguyễn Khoa (keys). With tight grooves, psychedelic textures, and a powerful, distinctive sound, SSR has performed countless shows across Vietnam, including major events such as Quest Festival, Vibe Nation, and Mui Ne Music & Art Festival. Saigon Soul Revival return – quite literally – in 2026 with “Chốn Ta Về” (THE PLACE WE RETURN TO), an album that represents both a musical and emotional homecoming. Producecd by Jan Hagenkötter and recorded once again in Ho Chi Minh City, the album blends Vietnamese musical heritage with contemporary global influences.

ai.en: Romare plays a live show at Band On The Wall. Archie Fairhurst's work builds new forms from existing material.

events.description: As Romare, Archie Fairhurst’s working practice is rooted in building vivid new forms out of existing material. Playful but also deeply researched, his albums and performances are patchworks of inspirations and obsessive lines of enquiry made from a global panoply of source material. The clue is in the name – Fairhurst called himself Romare in tribute to Romare Bearden, the lauded American multi-disciplinary artist renowned for his incisive collages. In Bearden’s process Fairhurst saw a way to approach the infinite pool of electronic music production with a more considered approach to sampling, creating music from existing sonic material and bedding themes into his juxtapositions. For all the considered concepts and unusual arrangements, Romare is dance music at heart, and it naturally translates into the live and club environment. At times Fairhurst has pulled together a full line-up to render his music on stage – a call back to his roots playing guitar and drums in bands – but elsewhere he’s at home sequencing and arranging his music solo, re-moulding album material in the moment with the flexibility which dance music so often requires. Equally, he has DJ’d prolifically around the world with an omnivorous approach which serves as a logical extension of his studio craft, balancing hidden corners of historical investigation with the kinetic impulse of the dancefloor.

events.description: Shabaka Hutchings is widely regarded as one of the UK’s most influential musicians and a defining figure in contemporary British culture. A bandleader, multi-instrumentalist, and producer, his work has reshaped global perceptions of jazz and experimental music through a practice that moves fluidly between jazz, electronic, spiritual, and diasporic traditions. In his solo work, Shabaka’s music reflects a deepening focus on breath, embodiment, and personal authorship. His 2026 album Of The Earth, written, performed, produced, and mixed entirely by Shabaka, marks a pivotal moment in his artistic evolution. Where earlier projects explored collective improvisation and a withdrawal from familiar forms, this work represents integration - uniting rhythmic propulsion, textural depth, and melodic openness within a singular creative vision. Drawing together the dance-driven energy associated with Sons of Kemet and The Comet Is Coming and the quieter, breath-led language of his recent solo explorations in Perceive It’s Beauty Acknowledge It’s Grace, his latest album, Of The Earth establishes Shabaka as a fully realised instrumentalist-producer. Created largely while travelling, the music is built from portable instruments and production tools, with looping rhythmic structures underpinning expansive choral melodies performed primarily on alto flute, alongside saxophone. events.description: Get ready for an unmissable roots reggae double bill. Featuring Culture (with Kenyatta Hill) and Cedric Myton (of The Congos), this is a rare chance to experience two true reggae icons who have carried the culture from its rise to the present day. The legendary harmony group Culture, originally led by the iconic Joseph Hill, gave the world timeless classics in the 1970s, including the seminal album Two Sevens Clash. Following Joseph's unexpected passing in 2006, his son Kenyatta Hill took up the microphone. With remarkable passion, a voice strikingly similar to his father's, and boundless energy, he continues to keep Culture's spiritual and musical legacy vibrantly alive. Sharing the stage is Cedric Myton, the distinctive falsetto voice and driving force behind The Congos. Their album Heart of the Congos, produced by the eccentric genius Lee "Scratch" Perry, is widely regarded as one of the greatest reggae records ever made. To this day, Myton is celebrated for his otherworldly voice, at once fragile and powerful, delivering performances guaranteed to send shivers down your spine. Cedric will be performing a set of songs from The Congos iconic catalogue.

events.description: Born in Rio de Janeiro, four-times Grammy nominee, singer, composer, arranger, and instrumentalist Joyce Moreno has in her portfolio over 400 recordings of songs she has authored, interpreted by the greatest names in Brazilian popular music: from Elis Regina and Gal Costa to Milton Nascimento, Sergio Mendes, and countless others. Beyond Brazil, Joyce’s work has been recorded by Annie Lennox, Wallace Roney, Omara Portuondo, Black Eyed Peas, David Sanchez, Jon Lucien, Claus Ogerman, Gerry Mulligan, Till Brönner, Flora Purim, to name a few. Joyce’s compositions have been featured in film soundtracks (e.g., The Player by Robert Altman and Legally Blonde by Robert Luketic), animations (the Japanese anime Wolf’s Rain, in partnership with composer Yoko Kanno), TV programs, and theatrical productions. In the early 1990s, her music was embraced by DJs all over the world, starting from London, and her tune "Aldeia de Ogum" became a massive worldwide dancefloor hit, with numerous remixes. Since the beginning of her career, Joyce’s registered trademark has been the first-person feminine voice, which she pioneered; she was the first Brazilian female songwriter to express herself in this form, opening the way for countless other artists who followed. Joyce Moreno has received four nominations for the Latin Grammy (2000, 2004, 2005, 2010), and numerous awards, worldwide and in her native Brazil.

ai.en: Leenalchi, a South Korean act drawing on traditional Korean storytelling, plays Band On The Wall.

events.description: Leenalchi’s music doesn’t ask to be understood, it asks to be felt. Drawing from the ancient Korean storytelling tradition of pansori, the band transforms centuries-old vocal forms into something urgent, rhythmic, and unmistakably modern. Their latest EP, Here Comes That Crow, pulses with hypnotic basslines, layered vocals, and playful sonic textures that blur the line between language and sound. Even for Korean speakers, the lyrics can feel elusive, but that’s the point. Meaning emerges through repetition, tone, and emotion, inviting listeners into a shared, almost instinctive experience. At the center of Leenalchi’s sound is composer and producer Jang Young Gyu, whose genre-defying approach has helped shape Korea’s contemporary indie scene. Backed by a dynamic rhythm section and four powerhouse vocalists, the group builds each track from the ground up, starting with groove, then weaving in fragments of traditional pansori narratives. The result is something like a psychedelic folk opera set to funk: theatrical, unpredictable, and deeply immersive. Live, Leenalchi are captivating. Their performances channel the raw, physical energy of pansori training, where singers learn to mimic the sounds of nature, from rushing water to whispered wind, into a tightly controlled yet explosive stage presence. Whether you understand the words or not, the effect is the same: a kind of musical storytelling that transcends language entirely.

events.description: Orchestra Mambo International is a powerhouse 13-piece Latin big band formed in late 2022 by salsa DJ Lubi Jovanovic (DJ Lubi) and trombonist/composer Jonny Enright (Grupo X). events.description: The Raghu Dixit Trio brings together three long-time collaborators – Raghu Dixit (vocals, acoustic guitar), Sanjay Kumar (guitars, bouzouki) and Akshay Ganesh (violin) – in an intimate new presentation of Raghu Dixit’s music. Known internationally for the exuberance and energy of The Raghu Dixit Project, Raghu now turns the volume down and the focus inwards. The Trio was conceived as a way to explore the songs more closely with a focus on journeying the audiences through the stories behind Raghu’s song-making and emotion that sit at their heart. Drawing from nearly three decades of song-writing, the repertoire moves between reimagined favourites from Raghu’s earlier albums, new compositions and unreleased material. Stripped back to voice, guitars, bouzouki and violin, the arrangements leave space for the songs to breathe and for the musicians to respond to each other and the audiences in the moment. It is a different side of Raghu Dixit: less about the spectacle, more about the songwriter; less about the full-band rush, more about the stories behind the songs. Raghu Dixit has spent more than two decades taking his music from Mysuru to audiences around the world, performing in over 50 countries and on stages including Glastonbury, WOMAD, Southbank Centre and BBC’s Later… with Jools Holland. ai.en: Nine Below Zero and Dr. Feelgood play Band On The Wall on one bill, two of the UK's best rhythm and blues bands.

events.description: Two of the finest UK Rhythm 'n' Blues bands on one incredible bill. Nine Below Zero released their classic debut LP 'Live at the Marquee' in 1980, the band kept the momentum going with 'Don’t Point Your Finger' in 1981 before releasing their third and final LP on A&M Records, 'Third Degree' (1982). Nine Below Zero toured with The Who and The Kinks around the time of this LP and also appeared on 'The Old Grey Whistle Test', and 'The South Bank Show'. Dr. Feelgood formed on Canvey Island in Essex in the early 1970’s and have enjoyed a string of hit singles in many countries including 'Milk & Alcohol', 'Down at the Doctors', 'Roxette', 'She’s a Wind Up' and 'See You Later Alligator'. The current line-up of Dr. Feelgood is led by their drummer Kevin Morris, and features Gordon Russell on lead guitar, Phil Mitchell on bass and charismatic vocalist, Robert Kane.

King Tubby protégé Scientist helped pioneer the dub genre in the late 1970's at Studio One gaining a reputation for his distinctive mixing style. Scientist soon became the prinicipal engineer at Channel One releasing a series of classic albums in the early 1980's such as Scientist meets the Space Invaders, Scientific Dub, Scientists wins the World Cup, Scientist Encounters Pac-Man, Scientist and Jammy Strike Back and Scientist Rids the World of the Evil Curse of the Vampires. Five of his songs from the album Scientist Rids the World of the Evil Curse of the Vampires were used as the playlist songs on the K-Jah radio station in the 2001 video game Grand Theft Auto 3. events.description: AGMP Presents THE STYLE COUNCILLORS 'Café Bleu' Tour The seminal debut album recreated live by the world's only tribute to The Style Council. The Style Councillors will be recreating the seminal debut LP by The Style Council, 'Café Bleu', along with all of the hits and classics in the finest celebration of Paul Weller's 1980's group where some of his best songs were recorded. After the dissolution of The Jam in 1982, Paul Weller joined forces with Mick Talbot, formerly of The Merton Parkas, Dexys Midnight Runners and The Bureau, to form The Style Council. The band released a string of successful singles between 1983-1989 such as Speak Like a Child, Money-Go-Round, Long Hot Summer, My Ever Changing Moods, You're The Best Thing, Shout To The Top, Walls Come Tumbling Down, A Solid Bond In Your Heart, Come To Milton Keynes, The Lodgers, Why I Went Missing, and more. The Style Councillors are a 9-piece band who were formed in 2013 by Darren Fletcher. Having quickly built a hugely loyal fanbase The Style Councillors are in big demand on the live circuit for fans of Paul Weller and The Style Council. An AGMP Concerts presentation. ai.en: Nouvelle Vague's A Date with Depeche Mode tour comes to Trinity in Bristol in spring 2027. The bossa nova project reworks Depeche Mode's songs on its seventh album.

events.description: AGMP Presents Nouvelle Vague, the renowned bossa nova project founded by Marc Collin and the late Olivier Libaux in 2003, are returning to the UK in style in Spring 2027 to celebrate the release of their seventh album, A Date with Depeche Mode. Nouvelle Vague are reinventing themselves again by dedicating an entire album to the repertoire of a single band for the first time: Depeche Mode. Thirteen iconic songs have been recreated and reinterpreted by new voices. Recorded in Rio with Brazilian musicians, the album establishes a dialogue between the musical soul of Brazil and Depeche Mode's timeless world, revisited with the Nouvelle Vague touch. The first single from 'A Date with Depeche Mode' is a duet of 'Enjoy the Silence' performed by Skye Edwards (Morcheeba) and Larry Love (Alabama 3) alongside Nouvelle Vague. Two voices, two worlds — one song. Recorded in Rio de Janeiro with some of Brazil's best musicians, the track strips back the Depeche Mode classic to breathe new life into it. Nouvelle Vague at their best. This bespoke tour by a band at the very top of their game is not to be missed. 10+ under 16 must be accompanied by an adult. events.description: Shakatak are one of Britain’s most enduring and distinctive jazz-funk bands, celebrated for their sophisticated blend of jazz, funk, soul and pop. Formed in London in 1980 by keyboard player and composer Bill Sharpe and guitarist Roger Odell, the group quickly developed a unique sound built around infectious grooves, melodic keyboards, polished musicianship and an unmistakable sense of style. Their breakthrough came with the instrumental single “Steppin’,” which became a club favourite and established Shakatak as an exciting new force on the British jazz-funk scene. Further success followed with “Night Birds” and “Down on the Street,” while the albums Night Birds and Invitations cemented their international reputation. Their music crossed effortlessly between the dance floor, jazz clubs and mainstream radio, earning them a devoted audience around the world. Throughout their career, Shakatak have remained remarkably prolific, releasing numerous albums and singles while touring extensively across the UK, Europe, Japan and beyond. Their sophisticated instrumental sound has also made them particularly influential in the worlds of jazz-funk, smooth jazz and contemporary groove music. Led by the creative partnership of Bill Sharpe and Roger Odell, Shakatak continue to perform and record, bringing the energy and musicianship that have defined the band for more than four decades. Their timeless compositions, distinctive sound and ability to connect with audiences across generations…

ai.en: Moses Boyd, a Mercury Prize-shortlisted drummer, plays Band On The Wall.

events.description: Mercury Prize-shortlisted, MOBO Award-winning drummer, composer and producer Moses Boyd returns with his first album in six years. Songs For Sinners is the record Boyd has been building towards since he first discovered music. A deeply personal body of work, it explores the push and pull of faith as something profoundly human – a force capable of comforting, dividing, unsettling and restoring in equal measure. Across an ambitious, vocal-led collection that fuses gospel, jazz, soundsystem culture, Caribbean rhythms, 808s and soaring choir harmonies, Boyd expands the language of contemporary jazz into something entirely his own. It’s a record that draws from the church he grew up in, the London soundsystem culture that shaped him, and the freedom of improvisation, asking what sacred music can sound like when it’s no longer confined by convention. His numerous live and studio collaborations include touring with Sampha and Kelsey Lu, drumming on Sons of Kemet’s Mercury-nominated album, working with South African Gqom king DJ Lag, producing Zara McFarlane’s Arise for Gilles Peterson’s Brownswood label, and collaborating with Little Simz and Four Tet. He has produced original scores for Louis Vuitton and Grace Wales Bonner, and co-leads Binker and Moses with saxophonist Binker Golding. His Mercury Prize-shortlisted debut album Dark Matter was released in 2020.

ai.en: RUTS DC present 50 years of The Ruts, celebrating their music from 1977 to 2027, at The Crossing with special guests.

events.description: RUTS DC present 50 years of RUTS Music (1977-2027) THE RUTS + special guests In 1977, The Ruts emerged from London with a sound unlike anybody else around them - the raw urgency of punk colliding with reggae, dub and rock, driven by formidable musicianship and a fierce sense of purpose. With Malcolm Owen, Paul Fox, Dave Ruffy and Segs Jennings, The Ruts created a body of music whose power has endured far beyond its original moment. After losing Malcolm Owen in 1980, the remaining members chose integrity over nostalgia by re-inventing themselves as Ruts DC, eventually losing Paul Fox in 2007. Ruts DC remain a living, evolving band to this day. But the time has come to celebrate the whole story. This tour is about taking the music that exploded out of a movement and bringing it onto a stage in 2027 with all its urgency and relevance intact. Music made across five decades - from the albums The Crack and Grin & Bear It, through Animal Now, Rhythm Collision, Music Must Destroy, and Counterculture? with the classic singles In A Rut. Babylon's Burning. Something That I Said. Jah War. Staring At The Rude Boys. West One (Shine On Me) and more. An AGMP Concerts presentation. This event is for over 18s only - No refunds will be issued for under 18s

events.description: Joy Oladokun is one of today’s most compelling genre-defying voices. Those themes remain at the heart of *Hope Is A Heavy Thing*, Oladokun's new 12-track album, due September 25. Produced by Oladokun with additional contributions from Nigerian producer Spellz and a feature from Nigerian artist Adekunle Gold, the album marks a bold new creative chapter, broadening her sound while continuing to explore questions of identity, resilience, and belonging with the emotional depth that has become her signature. The project further reflects Oladokun’s ability to draw from diverse influences while creating music that transcends genre and geography. Since her 2020 breakthrough, Oladokun has released three critically acclaimed albums, was nominated for Americana Artist of the Year, and saw her protest anthem “i see america” named a finalist for the Recording Academy’s Special Merit Award for Best Song for Social Change. Praised by *The New York Times*, *NPR Music* and *Billboard* for her ability to turn quiet introspection into lasting impact, Oladokun has brought her music to national television on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, CBS Saturday Morning, and Austin City Limits, while her songs have been featured across major TV series.
